# 2 Samuel Chapter 19 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folios 190r–191r | **Source Image:** source-texts/hebrew-OT/2SA_019_page_001.jpg, 2SA_019_page_002.jpg, 2SA_019_page_003.jpg

---

**1** Someone told Joab, "The king is weeping and mourning over Absalom." **2** So what should have been a day of victory turned into a day of mourning for the entire army. The troops heard that the king was grieving for his son, **3** and they slipped back into the city that day like soldiers ashamed of running from battle.

**4** The king hid his face and kept crying out, "O my son Absalom! Absalom, my son, my son!"

**5** Joab went into the house and confronted the king: "Today you have humiliated every one of your men — the very people who just saved your life and the lives of your sons, your daughters, your wives, and your concubines.

**6** You love the people who hate you and despise the people who love you! You've made it perfectly clear today that your officers and soldiers mean nothing to you. I'm convinced that if Absalom were alive right now and all of us were dead, you'd be just fine with that.

**7** Now get up! Go out there and encourage your men! I swear by the LORD, if you don't go out, not a single man will stand by you tonight. That will be the worst disaster of your entire life — worse than anything you've faced from your youth until now."

**8** So the king got up and took his seat in the gateway. When the troops were told, "The king is sitting in the gate," they all came and gathered before him. Meanwhile, the Israelites had scattered to their homes.

**9** Across all the tribes of Israel, people were arguing: "The king rescued us from our enemies. He saved us from the Philistines. But then he had to flee the country because of Absalom. **10** And now Absalom, the man we made king, is dead in battle. So why isn't anyone talking about bringing David back?"

**11** King David sent a message to the priests Zadok and Abiathar: "Ask the elders of Judah, 'Why should you be the last to bring the king home? The rest of Israel is already talking about it.

**12** You are my own brothers — my own flesh and blood. Why should you be last?'

**13** And tell Amasa, 'You are my own flesh and blood. May God strike me down if I don't make you my permanent army commander in place of Joab.'"

**14** David won over the hearts of all the men of Judah, and they were united. They sent word to the king: "Come back — you and all your men."

**15** So the king headed back and reached the Jordan. The men of Judah had come to Gilgal to meet him and escort him across.

**16** Shimei son of Gera, the Benjaminite from Bahurim, rushed down with the men of Judah to meet King David. **17** A thousand Benjaminites were with him, along with Ziba, the steward of Saul's estate, with his fifteen sons and twenty servants. They all hurried to the Jordan ahead of the king.

**18** They crossed at the ford to bring the king's household over and attend to his needs. As the king was about to cross the Jordan, Shimei son of Gera threw himself face down before him.

**19** "Please don't hold this against me, my lord!" he said. "Don't remember the terrible thing I did the day you left Jerusalem. Please don't take it to heart.

**20** I know I sinned. That's why I have come today — the very first from all the tribes of Joseph — to meet my lord the king."

**21** Abishai son of Zeruiah spoke up: "Shouldn't Shimei be executed for this? He cursed the LORD's anointed!"

**22** David replied, "What business is this of yours, sons of Zeruiah? Why are you trying to be my enemy today? Should anyone be put to death in Israel today? Don't I know that today I am king over Israel again?"

**23** Then the king turned to Shimei and said, "You will not die." And he gave his word with an oath.

**24** Mephibosheth, Saul's grandson, also came down to meet the king. He had not washed his feet, trimmed his beard, or laundered his clothes from the day the king left until the day he returned safely.

**25** When he arrived from Jerusalem to meet the king, David asked him, "Why didn't you come with me, Mephibosheth?"

**26** He answered, "My lord the king, my servant Ziba betrayed me. I told him, 'Saddle a donkey for me so I can ride out with the king' — because, as you know, I am lame.

**27** But he lied about me to my lord the king. You, my lord, are like God's own angel — do whatever you think is right.

**28** My whole family deserved nothing but death from my lord the king, and yet you gave me a place at your own table. What right do I have to make any more appeals to the king?"

**29** The king said, "Enough — I've made my decision. You and Ziba will split the land."

**30** Mephibosheth said, "Let him have it all! What matters to me is that my lord the king has come home safely."

**31** Barzillai the Gileadite came down from Rogelim to see the king off at the Jordan. **32** He was very old — eighty years of age. He had supplied the king with provisions during his stay at Mahanaim, for he was a very wealthy man.

**33** The king said to Barzillai, "Cross over with me and let me take care of you in Jerusalem."

**34** But Barzillai replied, "How many years do I have left, that I should go to Jerusalem with the king?

**35** I am eighty years old today. I can barely tell the difference between what tastes good and what doesn't. I can't enjoy food or drink anymore. I can't even hear the singers. Why should I be a burden on my lord the king?

**36** I'll go just a short distance across the Jordan with your majesty. There's no need to reward me like this.

**37** Please let me go back, so I can die in my own town, near my parents' grave. But here — take my son Chimham with you. Treat him however you see fit."

**38** The king agreed: "Chimham will come with me, and I'll do for him whatever you wish. Anything you want from me, it's yours."

**39** So all the people crossed the Jordan, and then the king crossed. David kissed Barzillai and blessed him, and the old man went back home.

**40** The king continued on to Gilgal, with Chimham accompanying him. All the men of Judah escorted the king across, along with half the men of Israel.

**41** But then all the Israelites came to the king and demanded, "Why have our brothers the men of Judah stolen you away? They brought the king and his household across the Jordan — along with all David's men!"

**42** The men of Judah answered, "Because the king is our close relative! Why does this upset you? Have we been eating at the king's expense? Has he given us any special gifts?"

**43** The men of Israel shot back, "We have ten shares in the king — our claim on David is greater than yours! So why did you treat us with contempt? Weren't we the first to talk about bringing our king back?" But the men of Judah were even more harsh in their response than the men of Israel.

---
*— PNEUMA*
